title: The Liquidity & Distribution Bottleneck
hypothesis: University past exam papers are trapped in chaotic WhatsApp groups, low-quality photos, and physical photocopy shops; organizing them into a unified web and mobile distribution platform will establish academic revision liquidity and test students' willingness to pay.
things_we_know: Kenyan university revision materials are intensely fragmented across ephemeral WhatsApp groups and student circles.
Campus photocopy shops sell faded, illegible photocopies for cash with long lines during exam season.
Students experience acute time scarcity and revision anxiety two weeks prior to end-of-semester examinations.

experiment.apparatus: Mobile-first responsive web app and native mobile distribution client, centralized relational catalog (School > Course > Unit > Paper), and payment trigger test.
experiment.method: Catalog foundational university units across engineering and sciences, seed verified papers, distribute access links through class representatives, and track organic download velocity vs willingness to pay.
experiment.variable_tested: Student adoption velocity, search latency vs WhatsApp scrolling, and conversion to paid access.

results.observation: Students rapidly adopt the platform because finding an exam takes under 5 seconds vs 15+ minutes in chat logs.
results.lesson: Instant zero-friction search and clean presentation break entrenched peer-to-peer distribution habits.
results.significance: Validates the primary liquidity driver of Paprz before expanding into paid solutions and native mobile app loops.

connection_reason: Validate: Per-paper micro-pricing (KES 3-5) to minimize payment resistance
title: The Per-Item Micro-Pricing Engine
hypothesis: Pricing individual academic papers at negligible impulse thresholds (~KES 5 for final exams, ~KES 3 for CATs) eliminates purchase hesitation while giving flexibility to introduce high-value content (e.g. project reports up to KES 100) later.
things_we_know: Physical campus photocopy shops charge KES 3–5 per printed double-sided A4 page.
Students resist large upfront semester commitments but spend small coins impulsively when stressed.
In JKUAT School of Engineering, past CATs and exams are exceptionally scarce and directly impact passing grades.

experiment.apparatus: Safaricom M-Pesa micro-billing trigger, tiered price catalog (CATs at KES 3, Exams at KES 5), and telemetry event tracker.
experiment.method: Release clean papers across 30 high-demand JKUAT engineering units; measure completion rate of KES 3-5 micro-purchases vs drop-off at payment prompt.
experiment.variable_tested: Impulse purchase conversion rate at KES 3 (CATs) and KES 5 (Exams) vs payment prompt abandonment.

results.observation: Students perceive KES 3-5 as practically free compared to the time and money of visiting the photocopy shop.
results.lesson: When digital price parity matches or beats physical photocopy costs, friction shifts entirely from monetary willingness to payment speed.
results.significance: Validates the initial monetization engine and establishes the stepping stone for premium KES 100 project reports.

title: The Web-to-Mobile Anti-Piracy Funnel
hypothesis: Deploying the web app strictly for search discovery and catalog proof, while enforcing in-app reading with screenshot blocking (FLAG_SECURE) inside a native mobile app, prevents WhatsApp piracy without sacrificing organic web search traffic.
things_we_know: Mobile web browsers cannot block screenshots, screen recording, or raw PDF cache inspection.
If a single student extracts a clean PDF, peer WhatsApp redistribution collapses the addressable market for that entire class cohort.
Students discover links primarily on the web (WhatsApp group links, Google searches for unit codes like SMA 2100).

experiment.apparatus: SEO-indexed web catalog with unit search and page-1 watermarked preview, paired with a lightweight native Android Flutter reader enforcing FLAG_SECURE.
experiment.method: Direct students from web search results to the native app to unlock full papers; track web-to-install drop-off rate vs external WhatsApp leak incidents.
experiment.variable_tested: Web-to-app install conversion rate and observed WhatsApp group leakage rate.

results.observation: High urgency and verified catalog proof on the web motivate students to download the mobile app to read the paper safely.
results.lesson: Public web discovery creates trust and demand; private native application runtime protects intellectual property and pricing integrity.
results.significance: Solves the academic piracy dilemma, defending per-paper monetization while maintaining organic web discovery.
